templateAdaptation: The audit brief targets a 20+ project polyglot monorepo (Swift 6.4/C#/.NET 10/C99/Python). This repository is one MQL5 product file plus three tool files. Non-applicable sections are documented in AUDIT/inventory.md section 6 rather than fabricated.

tasks.title: Build and self-test gates cannot execute: bundled wine64 is x86_64 and Rosetta 2 was absent on all four Macs
tasks.evidenceBefore: arch -x86_64 /usr/bin/true -> 'Bad CPU type in executable' on node1..node4; file wine64 -> 'Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64'; build-macos.sh exited 3 ('MetaEditor wrote no log') instead of 2
tasks.evidenceAfter: Rosetta install finished successfully; arch -x86_64 /usr/bin/true OK; wine64 --version -> wine-9.14; ./tools/build-macos.sh -> 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0
tasks.notes: Environment remediation on the audit host, not a source change. The underlying repo defect (the script cannot tell 'Wine cannot execute' from 'no result line') is filed as F-001.

tasks.title: No MQL5 formatter, linter, static analyzer, SAST scanner or coverage tool exists; gates are limited to compiler + census + self-test
tasks.evidenceBefore: No MQL5 tooling present in Homebrew, pip or the system toolchain; MQL5 is a closed language with no public parser
tasks.fixSummary: Documented as a tooling gap rather than a blocker. Compensating controls: MetaEditor compiler as the only analyzer, tools/census.py for dead-code/placeholder coverage, and manual evidence-based L4/L5 review recorded in the ledger.
tasks.evidenceAfter: AUDIT/environment.md section 2 records the gap and the compensating controls
tasks.notes: Not BLOCKED: a real substitute exists and is used for every finding.
